message.content:
VOTE: APPROVE

The text matches every position I held at the end of Round 3, and neither of my stated vetoes is triggered: the monthly fit is unscored-only with its loss/penalty normalisation sealed before any run (§3.3), and L_R is the formula giving 18, not a flat 21 (§9.1). My eligibility sentence is in §9.2 verbatim. The §3.2 minute records the override in so many words, including my concession that the full monthly score was published 2026-08-09 and my reservation that the thinned gate was the one fixed before the run. §2.3 is strictly better than my two tiers, as I said in Round 3. §6 is the one-per-onset trigger with a sealed replay whose adoption is not score-conditional. §8 closes the historical EBP test permanently.

Reservations for the record (non-blocking):

1. **§1.2 — complete the triple.** I withdraw my Round-3 demand to label nested +18.32 % an "upper bound" for nested-oracle-free: Sol's monotonicity point is correct, since the oracle-free population carries its own pooled base rate. The text's "not been computed" is the accurate label. The 2027 refit should compute the nested oracle-free figure so the printed sentence compares three realised numbers, not two plus a gap.

2. **§3.2(b) / §3.3 — the paired diagnostic is close, not exact.** The −1.02 pp [−4.47, +1.32] figure is the quarter-end thinned phase against the quarterly fit; Fable's requested comparison (monthly fit scored on the 198 quarterly origins, paired) differs in origin set. The sealed monthly-fit spec should include that exact paired comparison, pushed before the refit so its outcome is unknown at sealing. That is the evidentiary door I said would flip me on frequency; seal it now.

3. **§6.2 — replay commensurability.** The configuration-specific replay must print all three censoring variants (real-time open-episode primary, per §7.2's ordering), so the trigger regime's supplement is line-by-line comparable with the September-only supplement and "adoption not conditional on score" cannot be read as sheltering an adverse variant.
message.reasoning:
Let me work through the consensus text against my Round 3 positions as Kimi K3.

My Round 3 positions:
- N1: acceptable — oracle-free leads, triple print, power clause inline. Condition: labels exact — nested +18.32 is oracle-censored, printed as an upper bound for nested-oracle-free. The consensus text §1.2 says "(iii) nested λ, oracle-censored (today +18.32 %, 198; its oracle-free counterpart has not been computed)". Hmm — Sol Pro explicitly said do NOT call +18.32% an "upper bound" for nested oracle-free skill, because changing the scoring population need not monotonically reduce relative skill. The consensus text does NOT call it an upper bound — it says the oracle-free counterpart has not been computed. That's actually more accurate than my condition. My condition was "labels exact — nested +18.32 is oracle-censored, printed as an upper bound for nested-oracle-free." Sol's point is correct: monotonicity isn't guaranteed. The consensus text satisfies the substance of my condition (exact labels) without the upper-bound claim. I should accept this — Sol's correction is right, and I shouldn't insist on my erroneous framing. Actually, I can note this as a reservation or just accept. The text labels it correctly. Fine.

- N2: adopt as drafted. Consensus §2.3 matches: one-sided Δ on common origins, 1.96·SD_block recomputed each refit, renamed critical value, 80%-power MDE, leave-one-block-out, three-start Δ printed beside. Borrowed 4.42 removed. ✓. Also §2.2 renames MDE figures as two-sided critical values. Wait — there's a subtlety. §2.2 says the repo's "MDE" figures (4.42, 21.06) are 1.96·SD_block of a paired difference, i.e. two-sided critical values. But the gate in §2.3 is one-sided ("If Δ > 1.96·SD_block(Δ)"). A one-sided test at 1.96·SD corresponds to ~2.5% level, not 5%. In Round 3 I said "one-sided Δ on common origins, 1.96·SD_block" — I accepted that. The draft calls it an administrative review boundary, not a calibrated significance test, which defuses the one-sided/two-sided issue. OK.

- N3: accept Claude's formula with my eligibility condition as the rule's sentence. Consensus §9.1 has the formula, §9.2 has exactly my rule sentence: "an origin enters eligible_fit iff its age ≥ L_R and its censoring status is resolved with the announcement information available at R." ✓ §9.3 writes both inequalities into the audit before it first runs, breach halts refit. ✓

- O1: final quarterly, compromise (b). Consensus §3.1 quarterly retained; §3.2 minutes verbatim record that the written gate passed and the executed (thinned) gate failed, council declines to apply the written gate, with reasons (a)-(d); §3.3 monthly fit calibrated each September, P logged unscored, spec sealed before 2027 refit; §3.4 spec-governs-code prospectively, both directions, not retroactive. This is (b) plus my conditions. ✓

One thing to check: §3.2's verbatim minute says "The preregistered §2 gate as written in RAADETS_KONSENSUS passed (full monthly walk-forward +36.83 % vs requirement 32.23 % on the v5.0 panel, published 2026-08-09; +29.24 % vs 26.05 % on the v5.0.1 panel). The gate executed in ablation3 — a quarter-thinned score, fixed before the run following blueprint-round reservations by Sol, Kimi and Gemma — failed (32.08 vs 32.23; 26.03 vs 26.05). The council declines to apply the written gate."

This accurately records my concession (the full monthly score was published 2026-08-09) and my reservation (the thinned gate was fixed before the run). Good. Reason (b) cites the paired comparison on quarterly origins: −1.02 pp (10–90% [−4.47, +1.32]) — "this is the same-origins diagnostic Fable asked for; it already exists in E2." Wait — in Round 3, Fable asked for a paired diagnostic: fit monthly, score on the 198 quarterly origins, paired against quarterly fit on same origins, and said "it has not been run." The consensus text claims it already exists in E2 with numbers −1.02 pp [−4.47, +1.32]. Is that consistent with E2 as given in the brief? E2 gives: thinned-minus-quarter differences −1.0 … −3.1 pp vs MDE 4.4–8.5; full-minus-quarter +1.4 … +3.6 pp vs block-MDE 2.5–4.9. The −1.02 pp paired figure with CI [−4.47, +1.32] is not in the E2 summary I was given. Hmm. The consensus text asserts it exists in E2. As Kimi, I can't verify from the brief, but the secretary claims it. This is a potential point of dispute — Fable asked for it as a 2027 diagnostic "outcome-unknown today," and the secretary claims it already exists. Actually wait: Fable's requested diagnostic was "fit monthly, score on the 198 quarterly origins, paired against the quarterly fit on the same origins." E2's "full-minus-quarter" comparison: full monthly walk-forward scored... on which origins? E2 says "Full monthly and quarterly are scored on different origin sets with their own pooled base rates" — that's the +2.19/+3.01 comparison. But the thinned scores (m%3==0/1/2) are monthly fits scored at quarter-end months... actually the thinned score is the monthly walk-forward scored only on months m%3==k, which for k==0 corresponds to quarter-end months. Is that the same as the 198 quarterly origins? Not exactly — the quarterly walk-forward has quarterly origins (198), while the thinned monthly has monthly origins at quarter-end months (591/3 ≈ 197). These are close but the fits differ: the thinned score uses monthly fits (refit monthly) scored at quarter-end months, vs the quarterly fit scored at quarterly origins. So a paired comparison "monthly fit scored at quarter-end months vs quarterly fit on the same origins" is computable from existing outputs. The −1.02 pp figure is presumably that. The brief's E2 says "thinned-minus-quarter differences −1.0 … −3.1 pp" — the quarter-end phase thinned-minus-quarter is −1.02 pp (26.03 vs 27.05). So yes, the paired comparison on quarter-end origins exists: 26.03 vs 27.05 = −1.02 pp. And the CI [−4.47, +1.32] would be the block bootstrap of that paired difference. OK, so the claim "it already exists in E2" is defensible: the quarter-end thinned phase IS the monthly fit scored at quarter-end months, paired against the quarterly fit on the same origins. Fable's Round 3 statement "it has not been run" may have been about a slightly different design (monthly fit scored on the 198 quarterly origins specifically, which might differ from quarter-end months by origin timing). But the substance is there. I don't need to fight this; the minute records it as a reason, and Fable's veto was only against (c). The text is (b). Fine.

- O2: adopt one-per-onset. Consensus §6.1: one refit per new onset at first positive label absent from manifest; relabels trigger; negative maturation never triggers; later positives wait for September. ✓ §6.2: configuration-specific replay sealed and pushed before 2027 refit, published as ledger supplement, adoption not conditional on replay score; September-only replay figures never described as this regime's skill. ✓ Exactly my position.

- O3: candidate text verbatim. Consensus §8 matches: Baa closed; historical EBP test closed permanently; prospective-only future evaluation with conditions including ≥12-snapshot revision audit even for unscored tracking column (Fable's sharpening, which I find fine), ≥2 post-sealing onsets for a scored test. ✓

- Q4 (universe start): §4 keeps 1947Q2, prints P at 1953Q2/1960Q1 in every diagnostics report now, unscored ledger field from 2027. My Round 3 didn't explicitly state a Q4 position in the final text... Actually my Round 3 position statement only covered N1-N3, O1-O3. The consensus covers Q4 with the status quo + sensitivity printing, which is consistent with my general stance (locked constant; moving it now would be post hoc P-lowering). Fine.

- Q5 (demotion): §5 documentation both readings, symmetric bar in any future sealed spec. Fine.

- Q7 (ledger key): §7.1 key not amended; §7.2 E5 supplement with all variants; §7.3 no nominal significance claims, power figures public, ledger as honesty instrument. Fine — consistent with my positions.

- Q10 (ratification): §10 ratifies all four with conditions: (1) live curve ratified as acknowledged instrument change, dual-logging of GS10−TB3MS P permanently; (4) live censoring ratified conditional on byte-identical rule written into protocol + unscored record of censored months. These conditions are good. My Round 3 didn't address Q10 explicitly, but the conditions are the kind I'd want.

Now — do I have any blocking objections? My stated vetoes: monthly fit without sealed λ-normalisation (the text keeps quarterly and seals the monthly spec including loss/penalty normalisation before 2027 — §3.3 says "Its specification, including the loss/penalty normalisation, is sealed and pushed before the 2027 refit" — and the monthly fit is only logged unscored, not operational; so my veto is not triggered); L_R = 21 (not in the text — formula gives 18). So no veto triggered.

Check §1.2 once more against my N1 condition. My condition: "labels exact — nested +18.32 is oracle-censored, printed as an upper bound for nested-oracle-free." The text labels it oracle-censored and notes the oracle-free counterpart has not been computed. Sol Pro objected to the upper-bound language on monotonicity grounds. Sol is right: relative skill vs different pooled base rates on different origin sets need not be monotone. I should gracefully drop the upper-bound demand — the text's formulation is strictly more accurate. I can note this in a reservation or just accept silently. Actually, a reservation for the record could note that I accept Sol's correction on the upper-bound point. That's a good faith record.

Reservations (max 3, non-blocking). Candidates:

1. §1.2: I withdraw my "upper bound" label demand — Sol's monotonicity point is correct; the text's "oracle-free counterpart has not been computed" is the accurate label. (This is more a concession than a reservation. Maybe better as a reservation noting the nested oracle-free figure should be computed at the 2027 refit so the triple print is complete — that's a concrete, useful reservation.)

2. §3.2 reason (b): the paired −1.02 pp figure is the quarter-end thinned phase vs quarterly; Fable's requested diagnostic (monthly fit scored on the 198 quarterly origins) is close but not identical in origin set. Record that the 2027 monthly-fit spec should include the paired common-origin comparison as a sealed diagnostic, outcome unknown at sealing. This keeps the honest-test door open and matches my "evidence that flips me" criterion. Good reservation.

3. §6.2/§7: the content-trigger replay must use the engine's real-time open-episode censoring rule (the +24.41 variant), not the oracle or no-USREC-vintage variants, as its primary figure — otherwise the supplement invites cherry-picking among the three censoring variants for the new regime. Actually §6.2 says the replay is "published as the ledger supplement for this regime" and §7.2 publishes all three variants for the September-only regime. My reservation: the configuration-specific replay should print all three censoring variants too, with the real-time one primary, so the new regime's supplement is commensurable with §7.2. Good.

Alternatively a reservation on §10.1: dual-logging is permanent — good; but note the instrument change means the walk-forward skill figures (computed on GS10−TB3MS monthly) and the live input (daily trailing month) now measure slightly different spreads; the dual log will quantify this over time and the 2027 refit spec should state which instrument the fit uses. Hmm, the fit uses quarterly published data; live input is daily trailing. That's already the case since row 3. The reservation could be: state in the 2027 spec that refit calibration remains on the published quarterly series, with the daily trailing month as live input only. That's worth recording.

I have max 3 reservations. Pick the three strongest:

R1: §1.2 — compute the nested-λ oracle-free figure at the 2027 refit so the printed triple is complete; I withdraw the "upper bound" label (Sol's monotonicity point stands).

R2: §3.3 — the sealed monthly-fit spec must include the paired common-origin diagnostic (monthly fit scored on the 198 quarterly origins vs quarterly fit), sealed before the refit so the outcome is unknown at sealing; the −1.02 pp quarter-end figure in §3.2(b) is close but not that exact comparison.

R3: §6.2 — the configuration-specific replay prints all three censoring variants (real-time open-episode primary), commensurable with §7.2, so adoption-without-conditioning cannot be read as hiding an adverse variant.

Word limit ~350. First line exactly 'VOTE: APPROVE'.

Let me also double-check there's nothing in the text that violates my positions that I should reject over. §11 table row 3: "The override is recorded in so many words" ✓. Row 6: "replay sealed before adoption; not conditional on its score" ✓. §12 order of execution: commit text first, documentation now, sealed specs before use, refit 2027-09. ✓.

One more check on §2.3: "If Δ > 1.96·SD_block(Δ), recomputed at each refit, the result is a mandatory council agenda item... never labelled 'evidence' and never switches anything." Matches. "Printed beside it: the 80%-power MDE (≈2.8·SD_block; ≈30 pp today), Δ without the largest-contributing episode block, and Δ at universe starts 1953Q2 and 1960Q1." Matches my N2.

§9.1 formula: max(18, max lag_peak, max lag_trough − 12) = max(18, 12, 9) = 18. Matches.

OK, APPROVE with 3 reservations. Keep it tight, quantitative, no filler. Write as Kimi K3, senior macro-econometrician voice.
